compiled_state.description:
## Problem
Findings carry a `severity` string derived from impact alone (`severity_label(impact)` in
`review_kernel/decide.py`), which does not order the same way as the authoritative
`priority = validity x impact`. This misleads readers into treating severity as the gate
signal when it is not, and caused a real field misread (a finding read as INFO then MEDIUM
across identical runs when only impact drifted). This decision changes the Gerrit LLM-Review
comment format and touches two review gates, so it needs a recorded ADR before any of the
sibling implementation tickets land.

## Approach
Write `docs/adr/<next-number>-retire-severity-label.md` recording:
- the problem (impact-only label vs. validity x impact priority; the two duplicated
  vocabularies: kernel's critical/major/minor/none and findings.py's 5-level
  critical/high/medium/low/info);
- the decision: findings surface `priority` (numeric) + a `blocking`/`advisory` boolean tag as
  the canonical signal everywhere a human or a gate reads a finding; `severity` is removed from
  the finding shape entirely (BREAKING; documented in release-notes.md/CHANGELOG.md by the
  cleanup ticket);
- the migration sequence (rank aggregation by priority -> surface blocking/advisory in
  review-bot and CLI -> migrate `fail_on_severity` to a priority threshold -> drop the
  `severity` field), each landing as its own reviewed change;
- consequences: DET-tier findings (secrets detector, bugfix-size gate) get fixed priority
  constants since they bypass `pass3_decide`; `severity_label()` itself is kept as an internal
  impact-bucketing helper for calibration/eval use, decoupled from the Finding shape.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docs/adr/<n>-retire-severity-label.md` exists, follows the project's existing ADR
  template (see `docs/adr/0009-review-bot-pipe.md` for shape).
- [ ] The ADR names the four sibling implementation tickets by id and their landing order.
- [ ] The ADR states the BREAKING schema consequence and where it is recorded.
- [ ] `git grep -n "retire-severity"` finds the new ADR file, confirming it is committed
  under `docs/adr/`.

## Testing
Docs-only change, no code path exercised. Verification is inspection: the ADR file exists,
is committed, and is referenced by its sibling tickets.
